llm.summary: The SKILL.md expects many sensitive environment variables and local/remote tooling that are not declared in the registry metadata and there is no install provenance for the required binaries — the pieces do not line up and you should verify before installing.

dimensions.detail: The skill's stated purpose (publishing Naver blog posts via a local daemon/OpenClaw offering) could legitimately require local tokens and control-plane URLs, but the registry metadata declares no required environment variables or credentials while the SKILL.md references many (e.g., X_LOCAL_TOKEN, PROOF_TOKEN, OPENCLAW_OFFERING_EXECUTE_URL, ACP_ADMIN_API_KEY). That mismatch is disproportionate and unexplained.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The runtime instructions tell the agent to run local binaries under tools/ (preflight, setup_runner, publish) and to run an npx login command. They also instruct use of sensitive tokens and call local endpoints (/v1/local/*) and remote offering-execute endpoints. The instructions therefore access local daemon state and multiple credentials not declared in the skill metadata — exceeding what a simple 'blog writer' description implies.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill with no install spec or code files, yet it expects tools/ binaries and an npm package (npx @y80163442/naver-thin-runner). There is no provenance for those binaries or the npm package; relying on npx at runtime can pull arbitrary code. The lack of an explicit, trusted install mechanism is a material risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md references numerous sensitive environment variables and credentials (X_LOCAL_TOKEN, PROOF_TOKEN, SETUP_ISSUE_URL, OPENCLAW_CORE_API_KEY, CONTROL_PLANE_URL, ACP_ADMIN_API_KEY, etc.) but the registry lists none. Asking for admin/control-plane API keys or local auth tokens should be explicitly declared and justified; here they are implicit only in the instructions, which is disproportionate and opaque.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill does not request always:true and does not declare persistence. However, the agent-default ability to invoke the skill autonomously combined with undeclared access to tokens and remote control-plane endpoints increases the blast radius if credentials are supplied — so exercise caution.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Do not supply any API keys or tokens yet. Ask the publisher for: (1) a clear list of required environment variables and why each is needed; (2) provenance (source repo or signed release) for the tools/ binaries and the npm package @y80163442/naver-thin-runner; (3) an install specification or packaged release you can review. Prefer a minimally-scoped offering key (not ACP_ADMIN_API_KEY) and avoid giving control-plane/admin keys until you can inspect the code or run the skill in an isolated sandbox. If you must test, run inside a VM/container with no sensitive credentials mounted and monitor network/socket activity. If the author cannot provide trustworthy install artifacts and a clear justification for the listed tokens, treat this skill as unsafe to enable.
